owner: W1-10. The 87-weapon census of RI-WPN03 §A, with the per-weapon authoring that RI-WPN03 §B calls the inheritance model. Names are placeholders owned by the lore items (RI-LOR04); the COUNTS are RI-WPN03's and are binding as a per-class minimum.
why_lineages: RI-WPN03 §C caps SHARE(c) at 4 weapons per clip. A class of 8 therefore CANNOT have one shared moveset — a class-wide clip would be SHARE 8 and hard-fail. So each class is split into LINEAGES of at most 4 weapons, and every lineage authors all 25 mandatory slots as its own clips. Weapons then deviate from their lineage. This is forced arithmetic, not a design flourish, and it is why the animation reuse index for this roster cannot fall below ~0.32 whatever the builder does (see reports/W1-10-MEASUREMENTS.md §ARI). Two further constraints follow from the UNQ definition: a lineage may hold at most four weapons (SHARE <= 4), and a lineage containing a SIGNATURE weapon must hold at least three, because in a two-member lineage one member's override makes the other member's inherited clip unique and turns it into a signature as well.

delta_semantics.f: frame delta on startup and recovery of every r1.* slot. RI-WPN03 §B counts a parameter override only at >= 6 f@60, so values below 6 are stat-flavour and are NOT counted as DEV by the measurement tool.
delta_semantics.reach: metres delta on reach_m; propagates to the hitbox capsule length, so it changes the hitbox path.
delta_semantics.arc: degrees delta on arc_sweep_deg; counts as a parameter override at >= 25.
delta_semantics.root: metres delta on root_dz_m; counts at >= 0.15.
delta_semantics.hitstop: tier shift for this weapon's hitstop row: -1 one tier lighter, +1 one tier heavier.
delta_semantics.chain: delta on the one-handed chain length (adds or removes r1.4 / r1.5).
delta_semantics.ha: slot ids whose hyperarmour.enabled is flipped relative to the class default.
delta_semantics.mv / poise / stam: stat-only. RI-WPN03 §B excludes these from DEV explicitly and the tool does not count them.

shell.note: Knapped obsidian on a bone tang. The class reference.

thorn.note: Root-thorn: a hooked point that is drawn back through the wound, so every cut ends lower and further inside than the shell knives'.

wrapped.note: Bound linen and Hist-bonded talon alike. FST has four weapons, so it is a single-lineage class: two lineages cannot both reach the three members a signature weapon needs (see why_lineages).

reaver.note: Shorter, deeper-bellied raiding blades. They chop where a sickle sweeps.

duelist.note: Imperial duelling grip: side-on, deeper retraction, the point held higher between thrusts.

garrison.note: Imperial issue. The control against which every other weapon in the game is a deviation.

marsh.note: Marsh-guard pattern: shorter, carried low, cuts thrown from the hip rather than the shoulder.

gig.note: The fisher's gig. Underhand, braced against the hip.

lance.note: Marsh-lance: overhand, thrown from above the shoulder, the point coming down onto the target.

splitter.note: Shell-splitter. A wood-axe grip and a wood-axe swing.

hatchet.note: Short hatchets held near the head: flatter, faster, and they hook a shield rim rather than splitting it.

bogiron.note: A cast head on a straight haft. Everything arrives from directly above.

flail.note: A head on a chain. It cannot be stopped once started, so the arc is wider, the follow-through longer, and it comes round the side rather than down.

bill.note: The garrison bill. Hooked, swept low.

glaive.note: A blade rather than a hook: it cuts downward through a lane instead of sweeping across one.

hide.note: Plaited hide and living root-tendril alike. WHP has four weapons, so it is a single-lineage class, for the same reason as FST.

memorial.note: Barsaebic memorial blades. Ceremonial length, honest swings.

claymore.note: Imported Nord pattern: a flatter, wider swing with the hands further apart, and it travels further with the blow.

reaper.note: Reaper of the drowned. The full revolution.

scythe.note: A harvest scythe re-hafted for war: the blade tips downward and the spin ploughs rather than sweeps.

pile.note: The Xanmeer pile-driver. Straight down, every time.

maul.note: A quarry maul swung round rather than dropped: it arrives from the side and it takes the wielder with it.

golem.note: Root-golem's sword. Too big to be anything but committed.

zwei.note: A Nord greatsword pattern: held further up the ricasso, so it turns over faster and comes down steeper.

horn.note: Horn and sinew. Drawn to the cheek.

chitinbow.note: A chitin recurve: shorter limbs, a lower draw, and the shot comes from the chest rather than the ear.

weapons.name: Knapped shell-knife
weapons.line: The baseline. Twelve frames of startup and a metre of reach: the whole class is a question about where you are standing, and this is the plainest form of the question.

weapons.name: Bone awl
weapons.line: Its third light is a rising point instead of a cut — it comes up under a shield rim that the shell-knife's horizontal finish slaps off.

weapons.name: Reed dirk
weapons.line: The only dagger whose backstep attack is a cut rather than a stab, so it can punish two enemies stepping in together instead of one.

weapons.name: Thornfang
weapons.line: A hooked point drawn back through the wound: its heavy pulls the target a hand's width toward you, which is a spacing tool no other dagger has.

weapons.name: Hist-barb
weapons.line: Its rolling attack sweeps low instead of rising — the one dagger that comes out of a dodge hunting ankles.

weapons.name: The King's Needle
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Cut, then point, then point: the only dagger whose follow-ups are all thrusts, so once the chain is started it finishes inside a guard the shell-knife has to go around.

weapons.name: Wrapped fists
weapons.line: The baseline. Five hits deep at ninety centimetres of reach: the class is a bet that you can live inside everything else's minimum range.

weapons.name: Quarry caestus
weapons.line: Lead-cored: eight frames slower on every light and a heavy-tier hitstop, so the fifth hit of the chain lands like a mace rather than a fist.

weapons.name: Hist-bonded talon
weapons.line: The claws rake downward: its heavy hooks rather than drives, and it is the only fist weapon that opens a target's guard instead of going through it.

weapons.name: Marsh-claw
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Every hit in the chain is a hook, so the whole five-hit string turns the body over and over — it covers ground sideways where the wrapped fists stand still.

weapons.name: Naga sickle-blade
weapons.line: The baseline. A hundred and fifty-five degrees of arc on a four-hit chain: the light class that answers a crowd.

weapons.name: Tide falchion
weapons.line: Its fourth light is a rising cut that finishes above the shoulder and its third is an overhead, so the chain ends catching a rolling enemy instead of missing over one.

weapons.name: Mangrove hook
weapons.line: Hooked at the tip: it drags a shield down on the guardbreak instead of kicking through it, and it is six frames slower for the privilege.

weapons.name: Reaver blade
weapons.line: Short and deep-bellied: six frames faster and a third of a metre closer in, it chops where the sickle sweeps.

weapons.name: Saltmarsh sabre
weapons.line: Its running attack is a lunge rather than a pass, so it closes on an archer instead of going past one.

weapons.name: Kris of the drowned
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. It opens like a curved sword and then never stops turning: hits two, three and four are all revolutions. It fights standing still in the middle of a group, which is the opposite of everything else in the class.

weapons.name: Xanmeer needle
weapons.line: The baseline. Ten degrees of arc and two metres twenty of reach: it attacks from inside a guard the way nothing else in the game can.

weapons.name: Reed estoc
weapons.line: A quarter-metre longer than the needle and its third thrust drops to the thigh, so the chain ends under a shield rather than beside it.

weapons.name: Bog rapier
weapons.line: Six frames faster and shorter: the whiff-punish thrusting sword, built around the backstep rather than around reach.

weapons.name: Duelling pick
weapons.line: A spike rather than a blade: its heavy is an overhead pick, and it is the only thrusting sword that will break armour instead of finding a gap in it.

weapons.name: Oath of Salt
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Its chain alternates high and low thrusts, so it plays around a shield's height rather than its edges — the only weapon in the class that makes a turtle move its guard.

weapons.name: Imperial garrison sword
weapons.line: The baseline. Its r1 rhythm is the reference every other weapon in the game is a deviation from.

weapons.name: Kothringi bronze sword
weapons.line: Its third light is a rising cut rather than a horizontal, so it catches a rolling enemy that the garrison sword passes over.

weapons.name: Marsh-guard shortsword
weapons.line: Six frames faster on every light, fifteen centimetres shorter, and a fourth light attack: the closest thing to a dagger that is still a straight sword.

weapons.name: Barsaebic warblade
weapons.line: Its heavy is a thrust rather than a cut, and its two-handed heavy carries hyperarmour the class otherwise has nowhere — the one straight sword that will trade with an axe.

weapons.name: Oath of the Drowned
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. An entirely authored chain: horizontal, thrust, overhead. The only straight sword whose SECOND light is a point, so the chain steps inside a shield instead of going round it, and its heavy is a shoulder-level stab you can throw from behind your own guard.

weapons.name: Hist-sap blade
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Its weapon art is a committed lunge and its rolling attack is a spinning low cut with a 340-degree arc that no other straight sword has.

weapons.name: Fen-warden's sword
weapons.line: The longest straight sword at 2.15 m; its running attack is a leaping thrust that covers 1.30 m of ground.

weapons.name: Rusted levy sword
weapons.line: Eight frames slower to recover on every slot and a heavier hitstop tier: the bad sword that is genuinely different rather than genuinely worse — it trades where the others dance.

weapons.name: Fisher's gig
weapons.line: The baseline. Three metres ten of reach thrown from behind a raised shield: the class that wins by never being reached.

weapons.name: Reed gig
weapons.line: Its third light is a low sweep rather than a thrust — the only spear that clears a lane instead of picking one target out of it.

weapons.name: Mire trident
weapons.line: Three points: its heavy strikes low and its guard counter follows it there, so a blocked overhead is answered under the shield.

weapons.name: Marsh-lance
weapons.line: Overhand, from above the shoulder: the running attack covers over two metres and arrives point-first from a height a shield does not cover.

weapons.name: Root-pike
weapons.line: The longest weapon in the game that is not a whip: eight frames slower and a heavier hitstop, it holds ground rather than taking it.

weapons.name: Xanmeer sting
weapons.line: Short-hafted and six frames faster; it is the spear you take when you intend to be reached and want a whiff-punish waiting.

weapons.name: Harpoon of the drowned
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Its chain alternates thrust, sweep, thrust: it is the only spear that can hold a lane against three enemies rather than one, and its jumping attack is a dive rather than a chop.

weapons.name: Shell-splitter
weapons.line: The baseline. The best poise damage per stamina point of any medium weapon: one trade, correctly chosen, wins the exchange.

weapons.name: Bog cleaver
weapons.line: Head-heavy: six frames slower, a heavier hitstop tier, and its third light lands like a mace — the axe you take to a chitin-plated thing.

weapons.name: Marsh hatchet
weapons.line: Held near the head: six frames faster and twenty-two centimetres shorter, it hooks a shield rim rather than splitting through it.

weapons.name: Ridge axe
weapons.line: Its running heavy carries hyperarmour into the approach: the medium weapon that accepts a hit in order to arrive.

weapons.name: Shell-reaper
weapons.line: Barges rather than kicks, and its jumping heavy is a stomp: the axe built entirely around breaking a guard.

weapons.name: The King's Bite
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Horizontal, rising, overhead — a chain that climbs. The only axe whose light attacks cover three different heights, so a crouching enemy and a standing one are both answered.

weapons.name: Bog-iron mace
weapons.line: The baseline. The only class whose damage depends on what it hits: bring it to the stone thing.

weapons.name: Pilgrim's club
weapons.line: Six frames faster and wider on the third hit: the mace for a crowd of small things rather than one armoured one.

weapons.name: Bone hammer
weapons.line: Its guard counter is a round-arm blow rather than a thrust, and it hits at a heavier hitstop tier than its weight says it should.

weapons.name: Bog-iron flail
weapons.line: A head on a chain: the second light comes round the side and cannot be stopped once started — the only mace that ignores a shield's edge.

weapons.name: Root-maul
weapons.line: Eight frames slower with a pile-driver heavy: it is a great hammer that a one-handed grip can still lift.

weapons.name: The Stone Answer
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Three different blunt shapes in one chain and a bypass on stone deflection: this is the weapon a merchant sells you because you told them about the root-golem.

weapons.name: Garrison bill
weapons.line: The baseline. The widest medium arc in the game: it does not fight one enemy, it holds a corridor.

weapons.name: Fen hook
weapons.line: The hook pulls: its third light is a low stab that drags a shield away from the body, and its guardbreak does the same thing harder.

weapons.name: Reed partisan
weapons.line: Six frames faster with a thrusting second light: the halberd that fights like a spear until you need the sweep.

weapons.name: Marsh glaive
weapons.line: A blade rather than a hook: it cuts DOWN through a lane where the bill sweeps across one, its third light is a second low sweep, and its rolling heavy is the widest low arc any medium weapon has.

weapons.name: Saltcutter
weapons.line: Eight frames slower and heavier on impact; its running attack barges rather than passes, so it arrives already committed.

weapons.name: The Lane-Keeper
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Every light in the chain is a sweep at a different height. Three enemies abreast is not a problem it survives, it is the problem it was made for.

weapons.name: Hide-lash
weapons.line: The baseline. Three metres sixty and six poise damage: it will never stagger anything, and nothing can hold a shield against it.

weapons.name: Salt scourge
weapons.line: Six frames faster and shorter: the whip that can actually be used in a corridor, at the cost of the reach that is the class's whole argument.

weapons.name: Root-tendril
weapons.line: A living lash: it strikes straight down the line rather than coiling round, so it can be used with a wall at your shoulder.

weapons.name: Hist-bindings
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Coil, snap, coil, and a guard counter that wraps: the only whip with a defensive answer, which is the thing the class was defined by not having.

weapons.name: Barsaebic memorial blade
weapons.line: The baseline. The first class with two-handed light-attack hyperarmour: the weapon that asks whether you can commit.

weapons.name: Fen claymore
weapons.line: Hands further apart and six frames faster: it sweeps where the memorial blade chops, and it travels further with the blow.

weapons.name: Greatblade of the drowned
weapons.line: Its third light finishes horizontal at knee height, so the chain ends catching the roll that the overhead finish invites.

weapons.name: Tomb-guard sword
weapons.line: Eight frames slower, hyperarmour on the guard counter, ultra-tier hitstop: the greatsword that is really a hammer in a scabbard.

weapons.name: Reed bastard sword
weapons.line: The lightest greatsword; its backstep attack is a thrust, so it whiff-punishes at a range the class normally cannot reach into.

weapons.name: Saltwind
weapons.line: Its running attack is a lunge and it covers 1.7 m: the greatsword that catches a caster.

weapons.name: Oath of Ash
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Horizontal, rising, overhead, and a two-handed opener that is a full sweep — the greatsword that fights a group without giving up its trade.

weapons.name: Hist-greatblade
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Its third light is a full spin and its rolling attack sweeps low: the only greatsword that comes out of a dodge already turning.

weapons.name: Reaper of the drowned
weapons.line: The baseline. Three hundred and forty degrees: the hitbox passes behind you, which is the whole reason to hold it.

weapons.name: Tide falx
weapons.line: Six frames faster with a low finish: it gives up half the circle to be able to end a chain without turning your back on a second enemy.

weapons.name: Mire scythe
weapons.line: The blade tips downward: its second light ploughs rather than sweeps, and it is the curved greatsword that works against something on the floor.

weapons.name: Harvest-edge
weapons.line: Eight frames slower and one hitstop tier heavier; its running heavy barges through, which is how it opens a shield wall.

weapons.name: The King's Crescent
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Three revolutions in a row one-handed, four two-handed. It is the only weapon in the game whose chain never faces the same direction twice.

weapons.name: Xanmeer pile-driver
weapons.line: The baseline. The highest poise damage in the game: it exists to break the thing that will not break.

weapons.name: Bog maul
weapons.line: Swung round rather than dropped: six frames faster and it arrives from the side, so it cannot be walked out from under.

weapons.name: Stone-breaker
weapons.line: Eight frames slower with a second pile-driver in the chain and ultra-tier hitstop: the hardest single hit any non-ultra weapon has.

weapons.name: Root-hammer
weapons.line: Its running attack is a lunge rather than a barge, so the class's answer to a retreating enemy stops being 'hope'.

weapons.name: The King's Ruin
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Side, pile, overhead — three different blunt shapes, and a weapon art that is a whirl rather than a stomp. The great hammer that can be used against something that moves.

weapons.name: Root-golem's sword
weapons.line: The baseline. The longest commitment and the largest lunge in the game: it asks whether you can be right once.

weapons.name: Fen zweihander
weapons.line: Held up the ricasso: six frames faster, and its second light is a full-width sweep that the golem sword cannot turn over fast enough to throw.

weapons.name: Slab of the drowned
weapons.line: No edge at all: eight frames slower, blunt shapes throughout, and it bypasses stone deflection the way a mace does.

weapons.name: Salt-iron greatsword
weapons.line: The furthest-travelling running attack in the game at 2.8 m; you do not walk to a caster with this, you arrive.

weapons.name: Tomb colossus blade
weapons.line: Hyperarmour on the guard counter and the jumping attack: the only weapon that can trade while landing.

weapons.name: Oath of the Root
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. It opens with a sweep rather than an overhead, so it is the one ultra greatsword whose first hit does not have to be aimed at a single target.

weapons.name: Horn-and-sinew bow
weapons.line: The baseline. The only class with no melee grammar: it answers the thing that will not come to you.

weapons.name: Reed shortbow
weapons.line: Six frames faster to draw and four metres shorter in effective range: the bow you can use while something is already on top of you.

weapons.name: Marsh longbow
weapons.line: Eight frames slower and six metres further: the aimed shot that opens an encounter before it starts.

weapons.name: Chitin recurve
weapons.line: Drawn from the chest rather than the ear: it shoots flatter and hits harder on chitin, which is what it is made of.

weapons.name: The King's Horn
weapons.line: SIGNATURE. Every shot in its table is authored: the quick shot is a full draw thrown fast rather than a hip shot, which makes it the only bow whose fast option is not also its weak one.
